angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 634,622 km at 162.00 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.1728 +/- 0.0190 mas (same row, RUWE 1.19): 162.00 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.912206 +/- 0.095801 solar radii from Mayo et al. 2018, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-190 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....155..136M/abstract): 634,622 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.904597 +/- 0.032702 solar masses from Mayo et al. 2018, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-190 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....155..136M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5631 +/- 50 K from Mayo et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-190 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....155..136M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Mayo et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-190 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....155..136M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-190.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.474, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
